content.comment_body: [product_name] can be utilized with KNX/EIB via the [product_name] KNX/EIB module. I'm exploring if this setup fits home automation needs. For example, I have 16 light points and 16 KNX buttons, each paired one-to-one. The expectation is that every button connects to the bus, and [product_name] reads inputs from the bus, but only uses its physical outputs to operate the lights. My understanding is the KNX/EIB module mainly adds functionality. Based on module capacity, '[product_name] supports up to 24 digital inputs, 8 analog inputs, 16 digital outputs, and 2 analog outputs.' The base module offers 4 outputs, so reaching 16 requires two expansion modules. This provides 16 outputs and 20 inputs using the base and expansion modules. Since outputs expansion impacts available bus inputs, I believe only 4 inputs could be assigned via KNX/EIB, controlling 4 buttons for 16 lights. This seems limited. Is my understanding correct, or is there a way to deactivate the expansion module’s physical inputs and rely exclusively on KNX/EIB bus inputs? Additionally, with only 16 outputs available, expanding control seems restrictive. Is it possible to network multiple [product_name] base modules together using Ethernet (as master/slave), and have them share the same KNX/EIB bus? For instance, with two base modules (each with KNX/EIB modules installed and no expansions), can both connect to the bus and use the full set of available inputs and outputs?
Hello [user_name], for managing KNX integration, I suggest consulting application .vd files for the KNX Tool (ETS). These can provide useful guidance on setup and configuration.

Hello [user_name], please refer to the product manual for details. You can find documentation at [url], and page 16 outlines the available inputs and outputs, including Ethernet connections. For reference, '[product_name] Base Module supports the following connections for configuring the circuit program, no matter how many modules are attached: Digital inputs I1 to I24, Analog inputs AI1 to AI8, Digital outputs Q1 to Q16, Analog outputs AQ1 to AQ2, Network digital inputs NI1 to NI64, Network analog inputs NAI1 to NAI32, Network digital outputs NQ1 to NQ64, Network analog outputs NAQ1 to NAQ16.' Up to 8 [product_name] base modules can be linked on one network (using [product_name] communication) with either centralized or decentralized programs. The section covering the KNX/EIB module is on page 342.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are investigating how to combine [product_name] modules with KNX/EIB systems for home automation, aiming for direct correspondence between KNX buttons and lighting points. There is uncertainty about whether digital inputs from KNX/EIB can be used in place of physical ones and how output/integration limits affect overall system design, especially when expansions are added. Users also question if multiple [product_name] base modules can operate together on the same KNX/EIB bus to increase available inputs/outputs.
analysis.user_expectations: Users wish to assign digital inputs flexibly from either expansion modules or the KNX/EIB bus, ensuring sufficient capacity to accommodate all needed buttons and lighting points. They also expect that multiple [product_name] base modules could be integrated on a single KNX/EIB network to extend control and I/O capabilities.
